title: ctx-aead — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins protocol::aead_seal_ctx + protocol::aead_open_ctx byte mapping (XChaCha20-Poly1305 with CTX commitment outer per Chan & Rogaway 2022) AND every pub aad_* builder's canonical byte output. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output for raw key+nonce+plaintext+aad inputs), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per spec §6.4), 'aad_canonical_bytes' (per-builder AAD pin — verifies each of the 11 pub aad_* builder functions produces the canonical bytes, exercised independently of the AEAD primitive). Spec contract: docs/spec/protocol.md §5.1 (AEAD construction) + §5.2 (AAD assembly) + §6.4 (non-distinguishing failure).

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin aead_seal_ctx byte output for raw inputs

input_aad_hex.description: Raw AAD bytes (hex), variable length including zero. The aad parameter is the byte slice fed to aead_seal_ctx — vectors may use a builder-generated AAD (via the aad_canonical_bytes pins) or empty/arbitrary AAD for primitive-level coverage.

expected_sealed_hex.description: Ciphertext + 32-byte CTX commitment tag, concatenated. Length = plaintext.len() + 32.

expected_kind.description: Rust reference returns Err(ProtocolError::AeadFailure) — single non-distinguishing variant per spec §6.4. Ports MUST NOT distinguish wrong-key / wrong-AAD / tampered-ciphertext / tampered-tag beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome.

oneOf.title: aad_canonical_bytes — pin per-builder AAD output bytes (no AEAD invocation)

input_builder_name.description: Which pub aad_* builder function this case pins. Each builder takes distinct parameters; runner dispatches per name. aad_search_index_blob (MYND-29, §9.6), aad_workspace_blob (MYND-254, §9.7), aad_vault_indices_blob (MYND-271, §9.8) and aad_personal_dictionary_blob (MYND-266, §9.13) use input_account_number_hash_hex like aad_prefs_blob, with role strings 'search-index-blob', 'workspace-blob', 'vault-indices-blob' and 'personal-dictionary-blob' respectively. aad_quick_unlock_blob (MYND-329, §9.14.3) additionally takes input_provider_kind, appended as a trailing byte after account_number_hash.

input_kdf_params.description: Required for builder_name = aad_password_wrap | aad_recovery_wrap; absent for the others. Runner enforces per-builder presence.

input_items_key_id_hex.description: Required for builder_name = aad_vault_items_key_wrap | aad_note_item_key_wrap | aad_note_content_encrypt.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: Required for builder_name = aad_prefs_blob | aad_search_index_blob | aad_workspace_blob | aad_vault_indices_blob | aad_personal_dictionary_blob | aad_quick_unlock_blob.

input_provider_kind.description: Required ONLY for builder_name = aad_quick_unlock_blob — the wrap-key provider byte (0x01 biometric / 0x02 PIN) bound into the AAD as a trailing byte (§9.14.3).

expected_aad_bytes_hex.description: Canonical AAD byte sequence the builder produces. Implementations call the matching builder and compare byte-equal.
